content.thinking:
I'm planning the module structure for the bookshelf, deciding most parts can be plain objects without joints since they're static, but I'll still need a root joint at the origin to anchor everything since the builder likely expects at least one.

I'm sketching dimensions for the shelf frame — sides, top cornice, base plinth, back panel, and four shelf levels — and planning to use cel-shaded wood textures via grain paints for the surfaces, with flat gold trim colors kept minimal to stay within the color budget. I'm also setting up a helper function for creating boxes tied to the root bone, and starting to design a book-generating helper that builds a tilted cover with an inset page block for shelf decoration.

Still writing book geometry...

Rethinking the structure as separate boards with a visible spine and pages peeking out between them, since nesting boxes made the pages invisible. I'll build it as left and right boards slightly taller than the page block, plus a spine piece, so the pages show through the gaps.

I should cut the book count down to stay under the part limit, maybe around 36 books for roughly 250 parts, using a limited flat color palette (around 10 shades) shared between spines and boards to respect the 64-color cap, with cel paints cached per color for covers and flat gold for the bands. For leaning or stacked books, I'll handle the tilt by wrapping each book in its own group so rotation can be applied independently.

Rather than rotating individual parts (which wouldn't rotate the whole book), I need a helper that computes world positions using a transform: given a local offset and size for each sub-box, I compute the world center by applying the book's rotation and position, then build each piece with that placement. For a horizontal lying book, I'd rotate it 90° about the Z axis so the spine still faces forward while the height shifts to the x-axis and thickness becomes vertical.

Now I'm working out the shelf layout: inner width, shelf board positions and thicknesses, compartment heights between shelves, and overall unit height including cornice and finial details. I'm planning the structure piece by piece -- plinth dimensions and trim, then the side panels' sizes and placement.

For the back panel I'm considering a deep indigo paint with a scattered star pattern using a procedural cell-based function, visible only on front-facing normals. I'm then positioning the shelf boards at their respective height levels within the case.

Now I'm adding the top board, cornice, and gold trim line, then shaping the crown as a symmetrical ogee arch outline to extrude across the front for the pediment profile.

For the decorative finial, I'm considering a simple gold sphere at the top paired with a partial torus shaped into a crescent moon on the pediment's front.

For side ornaments, I'm adding thin gold vertical strips on the front edges of the side panels to act as pilasters, plus plane geometries textured with rune-like SVG patterns for extra decoration.

I'll make the runes glow faintly for a subtle magical effect, add gold trim boxes along each shelf's front edge, and sketch small triangular corbel brackets under the shelf corners using extruded outlines.

Still working out corbel geometry...

Now I'm planning shelf contents: bottom shelf holds a row of large tomes on the left, with a crystal orb on a stand placed center-right, filling out the lower compartment.

For the middle shelf, I'm adding a wicker barrel of scrolls, stacks of lying books with a candle on top, and an hourglass sitting between leaning piles of books.

For the top shelf, I'm laying out horizontal scroll cylinders in cubbyholes on the left half, with books and a small purple orb on a gold stand filling the right side.

Then for the final shelf and cornice, I'm adding tall candlesticks with glowing flames on each side, a small crystal cluster, and a candelabra topped with a glowing orb finial, plus floor clutter like a book stack with a candle, a scroll heap, and a pedestal orb on the right.

Now I'm setting up helper functions for building boxes, cylinders, and spheres attached to the root joint, along with a placement class that applies position and rotation transforms for local coordinates.

I'm also defining a color palette for book covers and a cached paint helper to apply them consistently.

Writing book-building function...

Positioning the gold bands symmetrically along the spine with the label plate tucked between them, and deciding to skip extra ornamentation like corner caps or rune emblems for simplicity.

For the label texture, I'm creating a parchment-style SVG with dark squiggle marks, applied to a small plane facing outward and positioned just in front of the spine so it inherits the book's rotation correctly.

Now I'm tallying part counts per book (8 parts, 320 total across 40 books) and working out placement logic for standing books on the shelf — positioning each book's center so it aligns consistently along the shelf depth with some jitter, then writing a row helper function that lays out a sequence of books with spacing and returns the ending x position.

For the leaning effect on the last book in a row, I'm computing the rotated center offset using a rotation about the z-axis pivoted at the bottom corner, adjusting the vertical position so the tilted book's corner lifts correctly based on its width and height.

Working out the lying-stack orientation now, figuring how to rotate each book so its height runs along x and thickness runs vertically, combining a yaw rotation with a 90° spine rotation to get the right world-space orientation.

For the candles, I'm planning cylinder-based wax bodies with drip details, plus a lathed gold candlestick holder defined by a profile curve revolved around its axis to get the brass base shape.

For the flame, I'm shaping a teardrop profile via lathe with a warm yellow glow core, layered with an outer translucent orange shell for extra softness.

For the orb, I'm thinking of a glowing crystal sphere in pale blue sitting on a gold stand with clawed spikes and ring bands, maybe adding a swirl texture pattern to suggest magic inside.

Writing SVG texture code...

Designing the scroll prop with a paper cylinder body, wooden dowel end caps with knobs, and a red ribbon band at the midpoint, considering whether to add a hanging parchment sheet with text for extra detail.

I'm settling on placing a hanging scroll draped off the front edge of shelf 2's board near x=0.38, as a flat textured plane rather than trying to render curled unrolled ends.

I'll add a mirrored star chart on the right outer side panel, and sketch textures for both: a parchment map with coastlines, compass rose, and dotted route, versus a dark star chart with constellation lines and gold dots. I'll also add painted stars to the back panel and a few glowing potion flasks on shelf 2, lathed with corks.

Writing hourglass geometry...

Still shaping hourglass geometry...

For the crescent moon I'm using a thin torus arc oriented in the XY plane with a gold glow. Now I'm adding rune ornamentation: a decorative plane across the cornice front with a horizontal SVG rune texture, positioning it on the top board and figuring out its sizing against the cornice geometry.

Writing rune generation code...

Checking stroke widths render at least 3px for visibility, I'm tuning cell size and stroke ratio for the frieze (44x1 cells) and vertical pilaster (1x40 cells) proportions to keep them within a sensible aspect ratio.

I'm also setting up wood grain paints for panels and shelves with different axis directions, darker tones for the plinth and trim, and a starfield-style back panel paint that layers a gradient sky with scattered star points based on cell distance and ID thresholds.

Next I'm thinking about floor details near the shelf's base—adding a flattened round rug with a dark red field and gold ring accent.

I'll place floor items like a book pile, orb pedestal, and candle cluster resting on the rug, making sure their base height accounts for the rug's thickness, and I'm double-checking the overall vertical bounds from the plinth up through the rug so nothing clips.

For the top, I'm adding a scaled-down pediment outline topped with an orb finial, with candelabra placed at the cornice sides and books scattered up top for that cluttered wizard-bookshelf feel, bringing the total height to around 2.33-2.5 units.

Narrowing the pediment's x-extent so the candles and books on the cornice edges don't clip into its sloped profile...

I'm adding gold decorative elements to the pediment front, a crescent moon and star, and now checking depth alignment across the cornice, top board, panels, and plinth so their front faces line up correctly.

I'm working out the shelf and back panel positions, then setting up a book color palette with dark variant pairs for each cover.

Now I'm tallying up rough part counts across the scene — frame, books per shelf, candles with wax and flames, scrolls, and orbs — to gauge how large the model will get.

Then I'm laying out the shelf heights and compartment spacing, followed by individual book dimensions and spacing for the first shelf row.

Adding a decorative orb with a gold lathe-turned stand and ring base...

For the right side I'm designing a wicker barrel using a lathed profile with a curved bulging body, topped with tilted parchment scrolls and gold hoop accents for detail.

Then for the second shelf I'm placing a stack of lying books at slightly different yaw angles for a natural tilted pile, topped with a candle and holder sized to sit right on top.

Working through the middle row placement, I'm laying out another cluster of books along x at varying heights and rotations, leaving a small gap before adding a trio of flasks and then an hourglass with a base disc, three thin support posts, and a top disc.

For the third shelf, I'm sketching a scroll rack on the left side — a frame with two shelf levels and vertical dividers creating six pigeonhole cells, with scrolls oriented horizontally so their round ends face forward.

Writing scroll geometry...

Still working out rack geometry...

I'm now placing the scrolls and books within each shelf cell, sizing scroll radii to fit cell height and positioning their centers with depth centered in the shelf, then laying out a small group of books on the middle shelf followed by a violet orb on a gold ring stand.

I'm adding a lying stack of two books topped with a cluster of candles of varying heights near the orb, defining their positions, colors, and whether each candle sits in a holder, then moving on to lay out the small books on the next shelf down.

Now I'm placing a tall brass candlestick, then designing a centerpiece open book on a stand—building the cover as a flat box and the two pages as thin boxes angled outward in a V shape to mimic open pages resting on a small pedestal.

Trying textured planes for page text seemed overly complex, so instead I'll fake text lines cheaply by painting stripes directly on the page boxes based on z-position, giving the look of printed lines across the open book's pages.

Now I'm scattering magical props around the scene: a glowing orb and rune ring hovering over the open book, a violet crystal cluster and candle to the right, a stacked-books finial with another candle on the cornice top, and on the floor a pile of lying books with a melted candle plus a pedestal holding the orb on the opposite side.

Also adding a scroll heap on the floor with randomly oriented scrolls laid flat, and defining a reusable candle-building helper that places an optional holder, wax cylinder, and dripping wax detail along the side.

Still shaping the flame lathe profiles, then tallying up the flat colors used across wax, flames, and other details to stay under the limit.

Designing the book label texture as a parchment background with ink rule lines and a gold dot accent, sized for a small rectangular svg.

I'm setting up a placement helper class that builds a point-quaternion frame so I can position and orient each book consistently in local space.

Then I'm writing a bx() helper that spawns boxes using these placements, making sure the color parameter type matches whatever Fill/Paint type the box part system expects.

I'm now computing book positioning geometry with lean angle, then writing a row() helper that lays out a sequence of book specs along the shelf, incrementing x by each book's width plus a small gap.

Next I'm working out a stack() helper for lying-down books, orienting each via rotation so the thickness is vertical and the length is horizontal, keeping the label face pointing outward, before moving on to code the actual shelf contents.

I'm checking types for outline points and planning a cylinder helper for parts with custom radii, height, and orientation, plus a trim function for gold detailing before writing the main frame assembly code.

Now I'm defining wood materials with grain textures for different axes, then sketching out the plinth box dimensions and gold trim bead placement, working through the panel widths and side positions.

Adding gold inner trim strips to the panel edges, then placing capital blocks and the top board to cap the pilasters, with a base block matching at the bottom.

Now I'm defining the back panel, then mapping each shelf's wood board with a thin gold strip along the front edge, and considering merging tiny scalloped stud spheres beneath each shelf into a single geometry for efficiency.

I'll place merged gold studs at the origin for reuse along shelf fronts and the cornice, add corbels under shelves 2-4, and position a finial orb with a gold base at the pediment's apex.

Then I'm placing cornice-top items: a candle on the left and a book stack with a glowing crystal on the right, verifying their vertical positions align with the cornice geometry, before working out the side panel orientations and coordinates for the case.

Working through the side wall maps, I'm positioning the star chart panel on the outer face with the correct facing direction so it's visible from outside, then sketching a circular rug on the floor whose extent is partially hidden behind the shelf front.

Writing rug paint logic...

Still designing the stand profile...

Adding crystal clusters with tilted glowing cones, then building flask shapes using a lathe profile for the body with corked necks and gold neck rings, plus a sparkle accent.

Now I'm setting up a rune texture generator, candle wax drips, a merged-geometry helper for decorative stud rows, and bead patterns running along shelves, cornices, and trim.

Next I'm building a scroll-prop generator with paper and ribbon colors, orienting cylinders along local axes using quaternions so the scroll racks sit correctly in 3D space.

Computing shelf1's row placement, then positioning a leaning book against it using the lean angle to offset its base so the top tilts toward the previous book, plus placing the glow orb and its stand at the right radius.

Still placing shelf items...

I'm shaping the candle holder with a lathe profile and sizing the candle height so the flame tip stays just under the shelf above at 1.86. For the open book I'm centering it at x=0.1 and placing a small magic mote hovering just above its pages.

Now I'm placing scattered floor items: crystals and a candle near x=0.38, a pile of stacked books with slight rotations near x=-0.8, z=0.4, a candle resting on top of that stack, and a stone pedestal with a large orb off to the right at x=0.8, z=0.45.

I'm adding a scroll heap and candle near the floor, writing a helper function to lay scrolls at an angle using rotated cylinders, then finalizing the overall height measurement and metadata export before generating the SVG texture for the map.

Still writing SVG code...

Writing book() helper function...

Still defining geometry options...

I'm adding the hourglass posts at three angles and sparkle motes using randomized glowing spheres, then auditing my imports to make sure I'm only pulling in the utilities I actually use—cel, mix, smoothstep, cells, mottle, paint, rng—and dropping unused ones like noise and INK.
